title: The Doppler effect and ultrasound

draft.title: The Doppler effect and ultrasound
card: The pitch of a sound changes when its source moves relative to the listener. As a source comes towards you, the pitch is higher. As it moves away, the pitch is lower.
A moving source bunches the sound waves up in front of it and spreads them out behind it. Waves that arrive closer together have a higher frequency, so the pitch is higher.
Ultrasound is sound with a frequency too high for people to hear. It is sent into the body, and some of it is reflected back from the boundaries between different tissues.
A machine picks up the reflected sound and turns it into an image. Doctors use this to look at an unborn baby or an organ without cutting the body open.
draft.remember: Pitch rises as a source approaches and falls as it leaves. Ultrasound echoes inside the body make images.

a.q: An ambulance drives past Sam with its siren on. What does Sam hear as it moves away?
opts: The pitch of the siren gets lower
The pitch of the siren gets higher
The siren gets louder but the pitch stays the same
The siren stays the same because its frequency is fixed
a.why: As the ambulance moves away, the sound waves are spread out, so they reach Sam less often and the pitch is lower. Higher pitch is heard only while the source comes towards the listener.
a.clue: Think about whether the waves are bunched up or spread out behind the source.

b.q: A clinic in Orange uses a scanner to make an image of an unborn baby. How does the scanner make the image?
opts: It detects ultrasound reflected from tissue boundaries
It detects ultrasound absorbed fully by the baby's skin
It detects sound the baby makes at a high pitch
It detects a change in pitch as the baby moves
b.why: The scanner sends ultrasound into the body and detects the echoes reflected from the boundaries between tissues. It does not rely on the baby making sound, and the image comes from reflection, not from a pitch change.
b.clue: Which option uses sound sent in and reflected back?

a.best: The pitch of the siren gets lower

b.best: It detects ultrasound reflected from tissue boundaries

problems.detail: The clue 'Which option uses sound sent in and reflected back?' gives the answer away: only one option mentions reflection, so a student can pick it without knowing how ultrasound imaging works.

b.q: A clinic in Orange uses a scanner to make an image of an unborn baby. How does the scanner make the image?
opts: It detects ultrasound reflected from tissue boundaries
It detects ultrasound that passes straight through the body
It detects ultrasound fully absorbed by the baby's skin
It detects high-pitched sound made by the baby itself
b.why: The scanner sends ultrasound into the body and picks up the echoes that come back from the boundaries between tissues. Sound that passes straight through or is fully absorbed never returns to the scanner, and the baby does not make the sound.
b.clue: Think about what happens to some of the ultrasound where two tissues meet.
